[2606.13644] Surflo: Consistent 3D Surface Flow Model with Global State Skip to main content Search Submit Donate Log in Search arXiv Press Enter to search · Advanced search --> Computer Science > Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition arXiv:2606.13644 (cs) [Submitted on 11 Jun 2026] Title: Surflo: Consistent 3D Surface Flow Model with Global State Authors: Antoine Guédon , Shu Nakamura , Nicolas Dufour , Jiahui Lei , Ko Nishino , Angjoo Kanazawa View a PDF of the paper titled Surflo: Consistent 3D Surface Flow Model with Global State, by Antoine Gu\'edon and Shu Nakamura and Nicolas Dufour and Jiahui Lei and Ko Nishino and Angjoo Kanazawa View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Geometry is invariant to viewpoint, which makes any collection of images a redundant encoding of a single 3D state. Existing feed-forward reconstruction models fail to exploit this: per-view methods emit overlapping, unaligned pointmaps that grow linearly with input count, while global-latent methods commit to a fixed, low-resolution output. We introduce Surflo, which compresses a variable number of unposed RGB views into K latent tokens-one global state-and decodes oriented 3D surface points by independently transporting them from noise onto the surface via flow matching. This frees the output from any fixed grid or token budget: the same latent yields from a few thousand to a million points in a single forward pass. To suppress the local inconsistencies inherent to independent per-point decoding, an inference-time guidance term correlates nearby points by injecting a photometric gradient during ODE integration. Surflo matches or surpasses feed-forward baselines on surface metrics, runs an order of magnitude faster than optimization-based methods that require hundreds of views, and is the only feed-forward approach to combine a global latent with arbitrary-resolution decoding. Variable views → one latent. Fuse N views into a fixed state of K=128 tokens. Decode at any resolution. Decode as many points as you want from one global state. Independent flow, coherent surface. While points flow independently, our guidance couples them. State of the art performance. Evaluated on 8 benchmarks, from 2 to 32 views. New surface dataset for real-world scenes. ~10.5K DL3DV scenes, full scene meshes. 01 Overview N input views N =  16 Encoder  E φ VGGT backbone  + Perceiver compressor Global state  z K = 128 tokens · fixed for any N Decoder  v θ Per-point Flow-matching ODE M oriented points M up to  10 6 Surflo turns a variable number of unposed images into a single global latent —not a stack of per-view tokens. Each surface point is then decoded independently , with a flow-matching ODE conditioned on that latent: we can sample any number of points from one encoder pass. We finally introduce a communication guidance mechanism relying on a shared rendering loss. At each step of the ODE integration, points are converted into 3D Gaussians and rendered with Gaussian Splatting. This rendering guidance limits disagreement between nearby query points. Global state. A Perceiver-style encoder compresses a variable number of views N into a global state z containing K = 128 tokens. Arbitrary resolution. The Flow-matching ODE, conditioned on z, decodes each query point independently, allowing for flowing any number of points. Coupling via guidance. A shared rendering loss lets points talk with each other during ODE integration. --> Global state. Surflo turns a variable number of unposed images into a single global latent —not a stack of per-view tokens. Arbitrary resolution. Each surface point is then decoded independently , with a flow-matching ODE conditioned on that latent: we can sample any number of points from one encoder pass. Coupling via guidance. We finally introduce a communication guidance mechanism relying on a shared rendering loss. At each step of the ODE integration, points are converted into 3D Gaussians and rendered with Gaussian Splatting. This rendering guidance limits disagreement between nearby query points. 02 One global state, One coherent surface Modern feed-forward 3D models — VGGT , DUSt3R, DepthAnything-3 — produce a pointmap per view . The representation grows linearly with the number of views, and leads to both noise and redundancy. Surflo encodes the entire image set into a global state   z  — one fixed-size representation, regardless of how many views you provide. From it, we decode a single coherent surface at whichever resolution we ask for. doesn't depend on the camera: the same surface, seen from many viewpoints. Surflo's encoder is built around exactly that idea, recovering the invariant Klein already pointed to: --> The result is a representation of geometry that, by construction, captures only what is shared across views . Geometry is what remains invariant under transformations of view. Felix Klein · Erlangen Programme , 1872 Surflo VGGT pointmaps Drag to compare — one shared latent vs N independent pointmaps. 03 Decoding explicit surfaces Each scene below is a Surflo reconstruction from 16 unposed images . For each scene, a total of 100K points are decoded from the global state before being assembled into a mesh. Points Mesh 8K points Points Mesh 32K points Points Mesh 128K points 06 Points communicate through rendering Independent ODEs are cheap and parallel, but two nearby queries can lock onto different surface ambiguities. We couple the points at inference time with a guidance mechanism: At each ODE step, we render the points with Gaussian splatting, back-propagate an image-space loss and update the velocities. The rendering gradient is the channel through which points communicate. no guidance Plain flow matching + photometric L 1  + DSSIM + monodepth expert Depth order regulariser 07 Comparison with state-of-the-art Drag the dividers to compare Surflo against VGGT and Gaussian Wrapping, the leading method for surface reconstruction from images. Surflo holds up even on tough captures with strong exposure variation and transparent objects — see for instance the translucent Totoro figurine in Scene 01. ## Model Description (Surflo)
Surflo (Consistent 3D Surface Flow Model with Global State) is a feed-forward 3D surface reconstruction model developed by École Polytechnique, Kyoto University, Kyutai, and UC Berkeley. It encodes unposed RGB images into a 128-token global latent state and decodes 3D surface points using continuous flow matching with photometric rendering guidance.
